arms.better: tm should turn the first ten inspection-only steps into a focused edit/test continuation instead of replaying essentially the same reads through three attempts. The user sees useful but repetitive `Ticket T-1 dispatched for execution.` and `Provider request failed. Waiting ...` messages, followed by failure text advising `tm --resume S-3` even though the run also schedules retry; that leaves it unclear whether to wait, resume, or run `tm ticket retry T-1`. Report aggregate tokens and elapsed time as attempts progress, and enforce a workspace filesystem boundary: this run executed `rm -rf /tmp/reproduce` outside the project. tm never produced a patch or ran task verification, so the passing result here is only the required mechanical post-run hidden-test check.

OpenCode could improve by avoiding the failed zvec lookup when this fresh clone has no index, and by checking its final test-count statement against the actual command output (it reported 152 tests while the crate's unit, integration, and doc-test totals sum to 153). A terse completion summary should also distinguish its own pre-overwrite regression test from the protocol's independent post-run verification.
